items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: If it’s people I don’t work with all the time, like Dave McKenna this weekend, I haven’t worked with him for a long time.

ctx.x: Depending on the band. I try to scope out a rhythm section right away. And if I can hear one guy, if the bass is turned way up, and he’s going to have it his way or no way, I’m not going to fight him. Because then we’re going to drown out everybody on the horns, and they’re going to be mad at both of us. So I’ll try and work with him. If he’s going to work with me, or if there’s no amp, or if everybody’s trying to make a group effort out of © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

it, then sometimes I’ll lead the way. I have to know who I’m working with. If it’s people I don’t work with all the time, like Dave McKenna this weekend, I haven’t worked with him for a long time. I listen to him. I didn’t want to put my foot on his chest and say okay, here’s where it is. I want him to be comfortable. If it’s someone I work with all the time, they know what I do anyway, and they’re probably going to wait for me to lay it down.
